title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammarNote:
Present Perfect vs Past Simple:

PRESENT PERFECT → прошлое связано с НАСТОЯЩИМ:
✅ Опыт: "Have you ever seen a snow leopard?"
✅ Недавнее: "I've just finished the report."
✅ Продолжается: "I've lived here for 5 years." (и сейчас живу!)
✅ Результат сейчас: "I've lost my keys." (не могу войти)

PAST SIMPLE → действие ЗАВЕРШЕНО в конкретный момент:
✅ "I saw her YESTERDAY." · "He called LAST WEEK."
✅ "She graduated IN 2022."

Сигналы:
Present Perfect: ever · never · already · just · yet · recently · for · since
Past Simple: yesterday · last week · ago · in 2020 · when I was...

💡 Ключевой тест:
"I've lived here for 5 years." = живу СЕЙЧАС → Present Perfect
"I lived there for 5 years." = больше не живу → Past Simple

rows.form: I haven't seen her this week.
Did you try kumiss last summer?
I didn't see her on Monday.
Have you ever broken a bone?
Yes, I broke my arm when I was eight.
Has she passed her driving test?
How long have you studied here?
❌ I have visited Almaty last year.
❌ She has won the medal in 2022.
❌ Have you finished it last night?
rows.example: ✅ Did you finish it last night?

grammarTip: KEY RULE: If there's a specific past time (yesterday, in 2022, last week, ago) → PAST SIMPLE. If there's no specific time, or the action connects to now (ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since) → PRESENT PERFECT.

exercises.instruction: Choose Present Perfect or Past Simple.
exercises.text: I ___ to London twice in my life.
exercises.hint: "twice in my life" = experience without specific time → Present Perfect.
"last year" = specific time → Past Simple: won.
"ever" = experience → Present Perfect: Have you ever…?

exercises.text: We ___ Amir at the tournament in March.
exercises.hint: "in March" = specific time → Past Simple: saw.

exercises.text: "She has won a medal in 2022" is correct.
exercises.hint: "in 2022" = specific time → Past Simple: "She won a medal in 2022."

exercises.text: They ___ (just arrive) — they're in the lobby now.
exercises.hint: "just" = recent action connecting to now → Present Perfect: have just arrived.

exercises.instruction: Identify the tense for this signal word.

exercises.text: Which sentence uses the correct tense?
opts: I have visited Almaty last week.

exercises.hint: "Ever" asks about life experience → Present Perfect.

exercises.text: Amir ___ (score) twice in last night's match.
exercises.hint: "last night" = specific time → Past Simple: scored.

exercises.text: "Have you ever broken a bone? Yes, I broke my arm when I was eight" — both tenses are correct.
exercises.hint: PP for experience question; PS for specific past event. Both correct ✅.

questions.text: Which tense do we use with "last week"?
questions.hint: "Last week" = specific past time → Past Simple.

questions.text: I ___ (never see) snow before this winter.
questions.hint: Never + past perfect, but also: "I have never seen snow" (Present Perfect) is fine in present context.
"Have you ever…?" = Present Perfect — asking about life experience.
"In 2022" = specific time → Past Simple: "She trained in 2022."
"Ever" = life experience → Present Perfect: "Have you ever tried…?"

questions.text: Amir ___ (score) twice in last night's match.
questions.hint: "Last night" = specific past time → Past Simple.
"Already" connects the past action to now → Present Perfect.

questions.text: She ___ (just finish) her workout — she's still at the gym.
Choose the correct response to "Have you finished your essay?"
opts: Yes, I finished it last night.
Yes, I have finished it last night.
Yes, I was finish it last night.
questions.correct: Yes, I finished it last night.
questions.hint: "Last night" in the answer = specific time → Past Simple.

questions.text: "She has won a gold medal" tells us WHEN she won.
questions.hint: Present Perfect does NOT specify when. If you say "She won a gold medal in 2022" that gives the specific time.

questions.text: In listening 1, how long has Rustam played football for the university team?
questions.hint: Statement 1: "He has played football for the university team for two years."

questions.text: In listening 2, what has Amir signed up for?
questions.hint: Listening 2, statement 1: "He has just signed up for a gym membership at WKU."

questions.text: Zhibek has done yoga since she started university.

opts: A person who has won a competition
questions.correct: A person who has won a competition
questions.hint: "Champion" = the winner of a competition; a person who is the best.

questions.text: The team showed great ___ — they lost three matches but kept fighting.
questions.hint: "Resilience" = the ability to recover and keep going after difficulty.
"Discipline" in a sporting context = consistent effort and self-control.
